checks.check: The new setting is explicitly a complex torus of dimension m>=1; the preceding section n>=2 assumption is not silently reused.
A constant reference metric on the torus is Kaehler and Ricci flat.
For m>=2 the previous integrated identity and curvature-sign average give S=0 pointwise, without assuming h closed.
A complex linear change makes the reference matrix identity and preserves lattice periodicity; its constant vector fields descend.
Multiplication by h converts S=0 to the symmetric first-derivative equation without a skew-torsion conclusion.
Fixing a barred column yields smooth complex-valued periodic coefficient functions.
The formal adjoints of constant complex derivatives on the flat torus are their negative conjugate derivatives.
Two integrations by parts and commutation make the cross term exactly the squared barred divergence, with nonnegative sign.
The expanded symmetric-gradient norm has two times each derivative norm and two times the cross term.
A sum of integrals of nonnegative smooth terms vanishing implies every holomorphic derivative of each matrix coefficient is zero.
Hermitian symmetry converts these vanishing holomorphic derivatives into vanishing antiholomorphic derivatives, so connectedness makes each coefficient constant.
In dimension one the coefficient of Chern curvature is minus h times the complex Hessian of log h.
The sign gives a periodic subharmonic log h; zero integrated Laplacian and integration by parts force constancy.
A constant positive Hermitian matrix has a closed associated form and zero Chern connection/curvature.
A finite unramified holomorphic cover is locally biholomorphic; curvature sign, closedness and zero curvature descend.
The conclusion is confined to tori and their specified finite covers; no extension to arbitrary Ricci-flat manifolds or novelty claim.
